o1.biggest_strength: It spots the in-app checkout bug as a ship-now fix, sizes the upside correctly, and then ranks tests around the real buyer doubts: delivery, size, firmness, EMI and trust.
o1.biggest_mistake: The last test bundles hero image and reviews, so a win would not tell me which part worked; the parallel testing plan also needs cleaner wording to avoid interaction problems.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Separate the image and review changes or make one clearly the treatment, tighten the test calendar/factorial setup, and add a simple ship rule for winners and guardrail breaches.

o2.biggest_strength: Very usable operator-style plan: it calls the bug first, gives the money, uses realistic detectable effects, and has clear rules for running and reading tests.
o2.biggest_mistake: It does not give firmness its own plain-language test even though firmness is 19% of chats; instead it spends one of the first five on a hero image test with the weakest evidence. It also invents calendar dates not supplied in the brief.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace or merge the hero-image test with a proper firmness/trial reassurance test, remove the invented dates, and keep the strong lane/sample-size structure.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because its first five tests better match the biggest customer objections on this page. Output 2 is a bit cleaner operationally, but it underweights firmness and gives too much space to a weaker hero-image idea.
